classes.1: selector-as-path — a name selector matches the wrong field
classes.2: scope-precedence — allow/forbid branch logic inverted or duplicated
classes.3: fail-open — an INCOMPLETE condition is dropped
classes.4: coverage-mask — coverage numbers hide an unenumerated source
classes.5: effective-set — a non-ELIGIBLE instance is treated as effective
classes.6: namespace-flatten — a namespaced name is matched on one segment only
classes.7: severity-downgrade — a P1 finding is demoted to P2
classes.8: canonical-order — the canonical key order is weakened

mutants.rationale: Name selector matches the scope string instead of the logical name: forbidden name 'deploy' would never match an instance in scope REPO, so DISABLE_MISMATCH never fires.
Forbidden-name set is hardcoded to 'deploy': any other forbidden name (e.g. 'acme:deploy') is silently ignored.
Allow-list check inverted: instances inside the allow-list leak, instances outside it do not — the exact opposite of the policy.
Forbidden-scope branch removed: a forbidden scope never produces SCOPE_LEAK.
else-if becomes a second if: an instance in a forbidden scope outside the allow-list gets TWO SCOPE_LEAK findings (extended case x11 pins exactly one).
Unknown-scope check dropped from deriveAuditStatus: an audit with unenumerated sources can report PASS/FAIL instead of INCOMPLETE (fail-open).
UNKNOWN-finding check dropped: an UNKNOWN finding no longer forces INCOMPLETE, so an unverified scope can hide behind a FAIL or PASS.
SOURCE_NOT_ENUMERATED defaults to CONFIRMED instead of UNKNOWN: the unenumerated source is reported as verified.
Coverage unknownScopes is always reported empty: unenumerated sources disappear from the audit result (S0 fixtures c11/c12/c13 pin non-empty unknownScopes).
enumeratedSources is reported as requiredSources: a partially enumerated audit looks complete (S0 fixture c11 has enumerated 4 of required 5).
DISCOVERED instances count as effective (ADR-006 violated): a merely discovered skill in a forbidden scope leaks (extended case x02).
DISABLED instances count as effective: a disabled skill in a forbidden scope leaks (extended case x12).
Name matched on its last namespace segment only: forbidden 'deploy' falsely matches 'acme:deploy' (extended case x03).
Name matched on its first namespace segment only: forbidden 'acme' falsely matches 'acme:deploy' (extended case x13).
SCOPE_LEAK demoted to P2: a scope leak alone no longer fails the audit (extended cases x01/x04/x09).
FAIL_OPEN_CONFIG demoted to P2: an unreadable config that fails open no longer fails the audit (extended case x07).
Canonical key order falls back to UTF-16 code-unit order: astral-plane keys (U+10000) sort before U+FFFF, breaking Python/Oracle parity (frozen vector astral-key-order-codepoint).
Canonical key order reversed: every multi-key object hashes differently (Python anchor {a:2,b:1} and the frozen vectors).
NFC normalisation of keys dropped: a decomposed key sorts by its raw first code point and canonically equivalent spellings hash differently (T011 regression test in the hash suite).
requiredSources is reported as enumeratedSources: the audit hides how many sources were required (S0 fixture c11 has required 5, enumerated 4).

note: 20 hand-written mutants in 8 classes. Each mutant changes exactly one rule in the frozen kernel; the kill test is the suite that must fail. A mutant is 'equivalent' only when it is provably behaviour-identical (none are expected to be: every mutant below changes an observable outcome on at least one frozen case). The runner applies each mutant to a throwaway copy of the repo (node_modules symlinked, real tree untouched) and runs the kill test there.
